# # Support Ticket: Internal Sentinel object leaks into Click callback

**Priority:** Medium
**Submitted by:** CLI Developer
**Product:** Click-based CLI tool

---

Hi support,

After upgrading Click to 8.3.x, our option callbacks started receiving a `Sentinel` object instead of `None` when no value is provided. Our callback code does `if value is None:` checks which now fail because it receives `Sentinel.UNSET` instead of `None`.

```python
@click.option('--format', callback=my_callback)
def cmd(format):
    pass

def my_callback(ctx, param, value):
    if value is None:  # This no longer works!
        return "default"
    return value
```

The `value` is now `<Sentinel.UNSET>` instead of `None`.

We need to know:
1. Which source files define and use the Sentinel object
2. The code path from option parsing to callback invocation that passes Sentinel
3. Whether this is intentional behavior or a bug

The repository is available at `/workspace/click/`.


Search only these repositories: github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1

Here is the full analysis:

---

## Findings

### 1. There is no `Sentinel` class or `Sentinel.UNSET` in Click 8.2.1

The repository `github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1` contains **no `Sentinel` class, no `Sentinel.UNSET`, and no named sentinel enum of any kind.** A search across all source files in `src/click/` yields zero results. The report that callbacks receive `Sentinel.UNSET` does not match this version of the codebase.

The only sentinel-style object in the codebase is:

**[`src/click/parser.py` L49](r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/parser.py?L49)**
```python
_flag_needs_value = object()
```

This is a **private, anonymous `object()` instance** — not a named `Sentinel` class — used solely to signal that an option was used as a flag without a value (e.g., `--opt` instead of `--opt VALUE`) when the option has `prompt` enabled but not `prompt_required`. It is resolved and eliminated **before** the callback ever runs (see below).

---

### 2. Source files involved

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| [`src/click/parser.py` L46–49](r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/parser.py?L46-49) | Defines `_flag_needs_value` sentinel; emits it during CLI arg parsing |
| [`src/click/parser.py` L436–455](r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/parser.py?L436-455) | Sets `value = _flag_needs_value` when a flag-prompt option has no argument |
| [`src/click/core.py` L33](r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L33) | Imports `_flag_needs_value` from parser |
| [`src/click/core.py` L2586–2588](r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2586-2588) | `Option.__init__` sets `self._flag_needs_value` flag |
| [`src/click/core.py` L2998–3033](r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2998-3033) | `Option.consume_value` detects and **resolves** `_flag_needs_value` → prompts or substitutes `flag_value` |
| [`src/click/core.py` L2268–2286](r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2268-2286) | `Parameter.consume_value` fallback chain: CLI → env var → default map → default |
| [`src/click/core.py` L2288–2337](r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2288-2337) | `type_cast_value`: if value is `None`, returns `None` (or `()` for multiple/nargs=-1) |
| [`src/click/core.py` L2348–2357](r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2348-2357) | `process_value`: calls `type_cast_value`, then invokes the callback |

---

### 3. Code path: option parsing → callback invocation

```
CLI args
  │
  ▼
parser.py: _OptionParser processes args
  │  If option used as bare flag (--opt, no value) and _flag_needs_value:
  │    value = _flag_needs_value   ← sentinel emitted here
  │
  ▼
core.py: Option.consume_value()                    [L2998–3033]
  │  if value is _flag_needs_value:
  │    → prompt user  OR  use self.flag_value
  │  else: fallback chain (env var → default map → get_default())
  │  ← _flag_needs_value is ALWAYS resolved here, never passes further
  │
  ▼
core.py: Parameter.process_value(ctx, value)       [L2348–2357]
  │  value = type_cast_value(ctx, value)
  │    → if value is None: return None             [L2292–2293]
  │  if callback: value = callback(ctx, self, value)
  │
  ▼
Your callback receives: None (when option not provided, no default set)
```

---

### 4. Is this intentional or a bug?

In **Click 8.2.1**, this is entirely intentional and correct:

- `_flag_needs_value` is an **internal implementation detail** that is resolved inside [`Option.consume_value`](r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2998-3033) and never leaks to the callback.
- When no value is provided for a standard option with no default, the full fallback chain in [`Parameter.consume_value`](r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2274-2284) returns `None`, and [`type_cast_value`](r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2292-2293) preserves `None`.
- **The callback receives `None` as documented**, so `if value is None:` checks work correctly.

The described `Sentinel.UNSET` behavior — a named public sentinel class passed to callbacks — does not exist in Click 8.2.1. If it is being observed, it is being introduced by a **third-party library, a custom Click plugin, or a fork** layered on top of Click, not by Click itself. The upgrade to "8.3.x" referenced in the ticket should also be verified: if such a class appears there, it would be a breaking behavioral change introduced in a version not present in this repository.
